File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or SHA1 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or MD5 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or SHA1 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35") or MD5 in~ ("f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f02a924c9ff92a8780ce812511341182c6b509d45bc59f3f7b522e37225d24fc", "d83fdb9e53c5ff03c4cb0451ea1bebd79b53f29eadc1e2fa394c7af13a86ce2f", "c7e9332731b06644fc73e0046a2a89eaa59b09f54250e9bd622467187351711f", "68257a6f9ff196179ec03624e849927f26599eb180a7c82e14ef5bc4e93bc309", "2ab684d93c1553fad87041b4dea97188a97e78589deee2a7bacff905564f3a35"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] File write of Talos top-prevalent malware hash to disk (drop site)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — A tale of two eras
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Execution of Talos top-prevalent malware (Coinminer VID001.exe / W32.Injector / Dropper.Miner) by hash · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Execution of Talos top-prevalent malware (Coinminer VID001.exe / W32.Injector / Dropper.Miner) by hash AIInstallation High
Hunts process executions whose SHA256/MD5 matches the four hashes Talos published as their top-prevalent malware for the week of 2026-06-11, or whose filename matches the named coinminer sample 'VID001.exe'. High-fidelity because matches are exact on hashes Talos has telemetry-confirmed in the wild. Rationale: Uses the exact SHA256 (9f1f11..., 96fa6a..., a31f22...) and MD5 hashes Talos published for Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, and Win.Dropper.Miner::95.sbx.tg in this newsletter, plus the named filename VID001.exe and the d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_NN_Exe.exe filename pattern that appears twice in the article (suggesting a dropper batch). No external corroboration needed — these are first-party Talos telemetry hashes.
ATT&CKT1059 T1496 T1055
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR / malware-analysis VM where an analyst detonates the sample on purpose
  • Red-team engagement using the published Talos hashes as a known-good test corpus
  • Backup software with embedded copies of quarantined malware (rare)
  • A legitimate vendor binary that happens to be named VID001.exe (extremely unlikely — verify via SHA256)
Suppression filter
and not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","malwarelab","detonation","-ir-") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cuckoo.exe","procmon.exe","procmon64.exe","any.run.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the full process tree on the affected DeviceId — parent of the matching process, child processes, and any DeviceFileEvents for the same SHA256 in the prior 24h to identify the drop site. Confirm the SHA256 against Talos reputation (https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation). Step 2 (contain): isolate the device via Defender Live Response / CrowdStrike RTR, quarantine the binary at the FolderPath returned, and reset the user's credentials if the integrity level was Medium+ or the parent chain included a browser/email client. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on SHA256 across the org for the prior 30 days; query DeviceNetworkEvents for the same DeviceId for mining-pool TLDs (xmrpool.eu, supportxmr.com, nanopool.org) and non-standard high ports; check DeviceRegistryEvents for Run-key persistence under the same InitiatingProcessAccountName.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where SHA256 in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or MD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
  or FileName =~ "VID001.exe"
  or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or MD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
  or TargetProcessName endswith @"\VID001.exe"
  or TargetProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, SHA256, MD5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Talos Top-Prevalent Malware Hash Match (Coinminer / Injector / Dropper.Miner)
id: 8c2f4e1a-7b3d-4f5e-9c1a-2d8b6e5f7a91
status: experimental
description: Detects process creation whose hash or filename matches the Talos top-prevalent malware list for week of 2026-06-11.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/a-tale-of-two-eras/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1496
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_hash_sha256:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507'
      - '96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974'
      - 'a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91'
  selection_hash_md5:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f'
      - 'aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9'
      - '7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376'
      - '38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98'
  selection_name:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\VID001.exe'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Internal IR sandboxing of the sample within an analyst VM
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Hashes:(*9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507* OR *96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974* OR *a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91* OR *2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f* OR *aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9* OR *7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376*) OR @Image:(*\VID001.exe OR *\vid001.exe OR *\VID001.EXE))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (SHA256HashData=/^(9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507|96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974|a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91)$/i OR MD5HashData=/^(2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f|aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9|7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376|38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98)$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\VID001\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\\[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, SHA256HashData, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") OR Processes.process_name="VID001.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376","38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") OR Processes.process_name="VID001.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
File write of Talos top-prevalent malware hash to disk (drop site) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the file-system drop of the same Talos prevalent-malware hashes regardless of subsequent execution — catches the staging step before the binary runs (or when it's blocked). The d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_<N>_Exe.exe filename pattern (appearing on two of the three samples) is a strong staging-loader hallmark and warrants its own pivot on the file-event surface, separate from the process-execution UC. Rationale: Pivots on the file-system surface rather than process execution — catches the drop before execution (or when AV blocks the run). Filename pattern d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_<N>_Exe.exe is article-specific: it appears twice in the list (the W32.Injector and Win.Dropper.Miner samples share the same 32-char dropper batch prefix), which is a textbook staging-loader naming artefact and a stronger signal than any single hash.
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike quarantining the sample writes the file to its quarantine vault — InitiatingProcessFileName will be MsMpEng.exe / CSFalconService.exe
  • Analyst saves the IOC sample from Talos's portal to a local malware-research share
  • Backup software re-hydrating a previously quarantined file during restore testing
  • FileOriginUrl pointing to talosintelligence.com indicates a researcher download, not a real infection
Suppression filter
and not InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe","CSFalconService.exe","CSFalconContainer.exe","SenseIR.exe","MsSense.exe") and not FolderPath has_any (@"\Quarantine\", @"\Defender\Quarantine\", @"\CrowdStrike\Quarantine\")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): inspect FileOriginUrl and FileOriginIP — if it points to talosintelligence.com or virustotal.com the writer is almost certainly a researcher; otherwise treat as a live infection and pivot to the URL/IP for delivery-channel investigation. Step 2 (contain): isolate the host, quarantine the file at FolderPath, and capture the InitiatingProcessCommandLine of the writing process — that names the delivery vector (browser, mail client, archive utility, LOLBin). Step 3 (hunt): query for the same SHA256 across DeviceFileEvents org-wide for the prior 30d, then query DeviceNetworkEvents on the same DeviceId for connections in the ±15 min window around the file write to identify the download source.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where SHA256 in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or MD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376")
  or FileName =~ "VID001.exe"
  or FileName startswith "d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_"
  or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, FileOriginIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileSHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91")
  or TargetFileMD5 in~ ("2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376")
  or TargetFileName =~ "VID001.exe"
  or TargetFileName startswith "d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_"
  or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^[a-f0-9]{32}_\d+_Exe\.exe$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") OR Filesystem.file_name="VID001.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_*_Exe.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_hash in ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91","2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") OR Filesystem.file_name="VID001.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="d4aa3e7010220ad1b458fac17039c274_*_Exe.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]

CodeIgniter4 application fingerprinting via /index.php route patterns AIReconnaissance Medium
Recon hunt for CodeIgniter4 instances exposed to the internet. Identifies CI4's default routing (/index.php/controller/method) and CodeIgniter-marker user agents/headers that precede CVE-2026-48062 exploitation attempts. Rationale: Article identifies CodeIgniter4 (composer:codeigniter4/framework < 4.7.2) as the vulnerable framework. CI4's default routing exposes /index.php/controller/method paths and the framework occasionally emits CodeIgniter-marker headers. The CodeIgniter docs linked in the article describe this routing structure. Cross-checked against: • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1595.002

  • Internal automated monitoring/uptime checks hitting /index.php health endpoints
  • Search engine crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot) indexing the application
  • Penetration testing tools (Nuclei, Nikto) authorized by the security team
  • Developer testing during application QA cycles

Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Determine whether the targeted hostname maps to a known CodeIgniter4 application in CMDB. Pivot on cIP/RemoteIP — is the source internal, a known scanner, or external? Pull CMDB vulnerability data for that host: is the framework version < 4.7.2? Step 2 (contain): If the source IP is unknown-external AND the destination is an unpatched CI4 instance, block the source IP at the perimeter and add the destination host to a watchlist. Notify the application owner. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot from the source IP to all DeviceNetworkEvents/W3CIISLog records for 14 days. Look for subsequent POST requests to upload endpoints (next UC) and any GET requests to .php files in writable/uploads/ paths.

HTTP POST upload with image MIME-type header but script-extension filename (ext_in bypass) AIExploitation High
Detects the exact CVE-2026-48062 exploit shape: multipart POST upload where the declared Content-Type is image/* but the uploaded filename ends in .php/.phtml/.phar. The ext_in rule trusts the MIME-derived extension, allowing a polyglot shell.php to bypass validation. Rationale: Article quote: 'an uploaded file named shell.php containing GIF-like content could pass validation such as: uploaded[avatar]|is_image[avatar]|mime_in[avatar,image/gif]|ext_in[avatar,gif] because the detected MIME type maps to gif, even though the uploaded filename extension is php.' This UC hunts that exact shape — multipart POST + image MIME header + .php filename — which is highly anomalous outside an attack. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate file-renaming utilities that mislabel content types
  • Browser extensions that mangle Content-Type during upload (rare)
  • Pen testers running an authorized assessment against the CI4 app
  • Misconfigured mobile client SDKs uploading thumbnails with wrong extension
  • Developer testing CVE-2026-48062 patch validation in non-prod
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("<approved_scanner_ip>", "<dev_test_ip>") and DeviceVendor in ("Imperva", "F5", "Cloudflare", "Akamai", "AWS", "Fortinet", "Microsoft")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full multipart body from the WAF log (FileName, FileType, Message). Confirm the filename extension is genuinely .php/.phtml/.phar and the declared MIME is image/*. Identify the target host — is the CodeIgniter4 framework version < 4.7.2? Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP at the WAF; quarantine the destination web host; preserve the request body and any file written to disk for forensics. If CI4 < 4.7.2 confirmed, take the upload endpoint offline pending patch. Step 3 (hunt): Search DeviceFileEvents/ImFileEvent on the destination for any .php file created in writable/uploads/ or public/uploads/ within +/-10 min of the POST. Pivot on file hash to find every other host that received the same payload. Search subsequent GET requests to that .php filename — those are web-shell invocations.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)([\?]|$)"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe", "wget.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "python.exe", "python3.exe", "java.exe", "node.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("multipart/form-data", "Content-Type: image/", "@filename=")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where isnotempty(FileName)
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)$"
| where Message has_any ("image/gif", "image/jpeg", "image/png", "Content-Type: image") or RequestContext has_any ("image/gif", "image/jpeg", "image/png") or FileType has_any ("image/gif", "image/jpeg", "image/png")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, FileName, FileType, Message, RequestContext
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP polyglot file written to web-accessible CodeIgniter4 uploads directory AIInstallation High
Detects creation of .php/.phtml/.phar files inside CodeIgniter4's writable/uploads, public/uploads, or wwwroot/uploads directories. Under CVE-2026-48062, ext_in validation bypass allows a shell.php disguised as a GIF to land in these dirs unaltered when $file->move($path) preserves the client filename. Rationale: Article quote: 'save uploaded files using the original client filename: $file->move($path), store uploads in a web-accessible directory, and allow PHP or other executable files to run from that directory.' This UC catches step 2-3 of that chain. The CI4 docs link in the article confirms writable/uploads is the canonical upload location. Cross-checked against: • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1036.008 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI4 framework updates dropping legitimate PHP files via Composer
  • Developer/sysadmin restoring web shells from backup for forensic analysis
  • WordPress/Joomla migration utilities copying PHP files into the same shared volume
  • CI/CD deployment writing legitimate application PHP files into the upload mount
  • Penetration testing engagement
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("composer.phar", "composer.exe", "git.exe", "msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull file SHA256 and pivot to VirusTotal/sandbox for verdict. Read the first 64 bytes — does the file start with GIF87a/GIF89a/FFD8FF/89504E47 (image magic bytes) followed by `<?php` later in the body? That's the polyglot. Identify the InitiatingProcessFileName — was the write by php-fpm/httpd/w3wp (suspicious) or a developer tool? Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the file (delete or chmod 000), block the source IP that triggered the upload, and disable execution in the uploads directory via .htaccess/web.config/nginx location block. Step 3 (hunt): Search DeviceProcessEvents for any process spawned by php-fpm/httpd/w3wp/nginx in the next 24h whose ProcessCommandLine or parent path includes the dropped filename. Pivot on the file hash to find every other host hit. Audit CodeIgniter4 version across the fleet; force-upgrade < 4.7.3.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/htdocs/uploads/", "/var/www/html/uploads/")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7|inc|pht)$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/htdocs/uploads/", "/var/www/html/uploads/")
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7|inc|pht)$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PHP file dropped in CI4 uploads directory then immediately executed by web server AIActions on Objectives High
Correlation detection: a .php file is written into a CodeIgniter4 upload directory, and within 30s the web server (php-fpm/httpd/w3wp/nginx) spawns a shell or recon binary as a child. Matches CVE-2026-48062 post-exploit: shell.php uploaded, then HTTP GET triggers PHP to fork cmd/sh/whoami. Rationale: Article quote: 'In those conditions, this may lead to arbitrary code execution.' That ACE happens when the uploaded shell.php is invoked over HTTP — php-fpm/httpd executes the polyglot, which forks a shell for recon. The 30s window tightly couples upload to first execution, which is the strongest signal that the upload was malicious rather than benign content. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PHP application that intentionally exec's shell (image conversion via ImageMagick, ffmpeg wrapper)
  • Pen-test of the just-deployed CI4 patch validation
  • Developer running diagnostic PHP scripts in dev/staging that exec whoami
  • WordPress/CMS plugins that shell out to system binaries (ClamAV scan, gif optimization)
  • Backup utilities running PHP-driven file sweeps
Suppression filter
| where ChildProcess !in~ ("convert.exe", "ffmpeg.exe", "clamscan.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Read the DroppedFile contents — confirm polyglot (image magic + `<?php`). Pull the DelaySec — sub-5s strongly suggests the attacker triggered it; 20-30s suggests scanner or automated PoC. Pivot on WebServer's SourceIP from web logs for the corresponding GET. Step 2 (contain): Kill the ChildProcess (DeviceProcessEvents has ProcessId), quarantine DroppedFile, isolate the host from network if shell egress observed. Block source IP at perimeter. If CI4 < 4.7.3, take the upload endpoint offline. Step 3 (hunt): Pull all DeviceNetworkEvents for the ChildProcess for 7 days — outbound C2? Pull all DeviceFileEvents in the upload dir for 30d to find every other dropped polyglot. Audit the database (mysqld/mariadb) for new admin accounts created by the web shell.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let UploadDirs = dynamic([@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/var/www/html/uploads/"]);
let WebServers = dynamic(["php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "httpd.exe", "w3wp.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2", "httpd", "php-fpm", "nginx"]);
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "nc.exe", "ncat.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "curl.exe", "wget.exe", "whoami", "id", "uname"]);
let FileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FolderPath has_any (UploadDirs)
    | where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)$"
    | project FileWriteTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DroppedFile = strcat(FolderPath, FileName), DropperProc = InitiatingProcessFileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any (WebServers)
| where FileName has_any (ShellChildren) or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("whoami", "uname -a", "id;", "cat /etc/passwd", "net user", "hostname")
| join kind=inner FileWrites on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (FileWriteTime .. FileWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project FileWriteTime, ExecTime = Timestamp, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, FileWriteTime), DeviceName, DroppedFile, DropperProc, WebServer = InitiatingProcessFileName, ChildProcess = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, AccountName
| order by ExecTime desc

let WindowSeconds = 30;
let UploadDirs = dynamic([@"\writable\uploads\", "/writable/uploads/", @"\public\uploads\", "/public/uploads/", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\uploads\", "/var/www/html/uploads/"]);
let WebServers = dynamic(["php-fpm.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "httpd.exe", "w3wp.exe", "nginx.exe", "apache2", "httpd", "php-fpm", "nginx"]);
let ShellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "nc.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe"]);
let FileWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (UploadDirs)
    | where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)$"
    | project FileWriteTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DroppedFile = TargetFilePath;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (WebServers)
| where TargetProcessName has_any (ShellChildren) or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("whoami", "uname -a", "id;", "cat /etc/passwd")
| join kind=inner FileWrites on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (FileWriteTime .. FileWriteTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| project FileWriteTime, ExecTime = TimeGenerated, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, FileWriteTime), DvcHostname, DroppedFile, WebServer = ParentProcessName, ChildProcess = TargetProcessName, ChildCmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by ExecTime desc
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|httpd|w3wp|nginx|apache2)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|sh|bash|nc|ncat|whoami|net)\.exe$|\/(sh|bash|dash|nc|whoami|id|uname)$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten | regex("(?i)(/writable/uploads/|\\\\writable\\\\uploads\\\\|/public/uploads/|\\\\public\\\\uploads\\\\)", field=TargetFileName) | TargetFileName=/\.(php|phtml|phar)$/i}, field=aid, include=[TargetFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, TargetFileName], function=count())

    | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Direct HTTP GET to PHP file inside CodeIgniter4 uploads directory AIActions on Objectives High
Detects web traffic invoking a .php file that lives under writable/uploads or public/uploads — the post-exploit shell access vector for CVE-2026-48062. Legitimate CI4 apps NEVER serve PHP from these directories; any GET to them is high-fidelity web-shell signal. Rationale: Article workflow: shell.php is uploaded under writable/uploads, then 'allow PHP or other executable files to run from that directory' leads to ACE. The next attacker step is an HTTP request to that file. CodeIgniter4 docs explicitly recommend `writable/uploads` as the canonical upload path — making this directory + .php pairing entirely abnormal in healthy CI4 deployments. Cross-checked against: • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate CodeIgniter4 modules that intentionally route through /uploads/ (very rare, itself a misconfiguration)
  • 404 probe noise from scanners (filterable on scStatus 404)
  • Pen-test engagement against the patched application
  • Asset discovery scanners (Nuclei, Burp) authorized by IT
  • Developer manually testing the upload feature in production
Suppression filter
| where scStatus != 404 and cIP !in ("<approved_scanner_ip>", "<security_team_ip>")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Check scStatus — 200 means the shell answered, 404 means nothing landed. Pull the cIP and check whether it matches the source IP of the upload POST that preceded it. Identify the csUriStem filename and pivot to DeviceFileEvents to confirm the file exists on disk and review its contents (polyglot check). Step 2 (contain): Block cIP at the WAF/firewall, delete the .php from disk, take the affected CI4 app offline if scStatus 200 (confirmed RCE), preserve web logs and the file. If still vulnerable, force-upgrade CI4 to 4.7.3+. Step 3 (hunt): Pull every csUriStem the cIP hit in the last 14 days — look for other web shells the actor planted. Pivot on csUserAgent for matching scans against other CI4 hosts. Search DeviceProcessEvents for any cmd/sh spawned by the web server in the 5 minutes around the scStatus 200 hit.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)/(writable|public)/?uploads?/[^/]+\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)([\?]|$)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP, LocalPort
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod in ("GET", "POST")
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/(writable|public)/?uploads?/[^/]+\.(php|phtml|phar|php5|php7)$"
| project TimeGenerated, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, scStatus, csUserAgent, csUserName, TimeTaken
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Nx s1ngularity 'telemetry.js' postinstall payload execution AIExploitation High
Detects execution of the telemetry.js postinstall script associated with the Nx s1ngularity npm supply-chain compromise (Aug 2025). The script is invoked by npm during install, scrapes GitHub/npm tokens, SSH keys and crypto wallets, and exfiltrates them to attacker-created public GitHub repos. Rationale: Anchored on the article-named 'telemetry.js' postinstall script and 's1ngularity' brand string. Cross-checked at the Nx post-mortem (nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem) and Datadog Security Labs which both confirm telemetry.js as the canonical Nx-poisoned filename invoked from package.json's postinstall hook. Parent-filename narrowing to JS package managers removes the obvious FP shape. Cross-checked against: • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/learnings-from-recent-npm-compromises/ • https://snyk.io/blog/weaponizing-ai-coding-agents-for-malware-in-the-nx-malicious-package/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Nx packages published before/after the malicious window — current versions of @nx/* may still ship a benign telemetry.js
  • Developer hand-running 'node scripts/telemetry.js' in a non-Nx repo unrelated to npm install
  • Internal monorepo with a homegrown telemetry.js used in pre/post hooks
  • CI runners that pin to a known-clean Nx version but still surface the filename
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\@nrwl\\nx\\","\\node_modules\\nx\\") and SHA256 in ("<known-good-nx-sha256>"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the full ProcessCreate row + parent cmdline; confirm the parent is an active 'npm install' or 'yarn add' invocation and not a manual 'node telemetry.js' run. Pivot DeviceFileEvents for SHA256 of the telemetry.js file under node_modules. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the device via Defender Live Response, revoke the user's GitHub PAT, npm token, and any AWS keys from ~/.aws/credentials, and rotate SSH keys touched on that host. 3) HUNT: search for outbound connections to api.github.com creating 's1ngularity-repository*' under the user's GH account, query DeviceFileEvents for 'results.b64' across the fleet, and review npm audit log for which package version dragged it in.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity","@nrwl/nx","nx-cloud")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "telemetry.js" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity","@nrwl/nx","nx-cloud")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TruffleHog secret scanner spawned by Node/npm (Shai-Hulud worm pattern) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the TruffleHog secret-scanning binary being launched as a child of node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun. The Shai-Hulud worm installs the Bun runtime mid-install and uses TruffleHog to scrape API keys, tokens, and cloud credentials from the host before pushing them to a hardcoded webhook. Rationale: Article explicitly names TruffleHog as the Shai-Hulud credential-harvest tool. Sysdig and ReversingLabs both confirm trufflehog is fetched + executed under npm install context. Pairing the binary signal with a JS-package-manager parent eliminates the legit dev/CI TruffleHog runs (which are launched from CI YAML or the user shell, not from node). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://checkmarx.com/zero-post/inside-shai-huluds-maw-how-the-npm-worm-exploits-and-propagates/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Pre-commit hook calling 'npx trufflehog' as legitimate secret scanning (common in modern dev workflows)
  • GitHub Actions self-hosted runner with the trufflehog action where the workflow shell parent is node
  • CI orchestrator that wraps trufflehog in a node-based runner like 'turbo run'
  • Security researcher hand-running 'npx trufflehog filesystem .' against a repo
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pre-commit","husky","lint-staged") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git-secrets","pre-commit"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull TruffleHog cmdline — Shai-Hulud invokes with '--json' and filesystem/git scopes targeting $HOME and common cred dirs. Check whether the parent chain includes an in-flight 'npm install' / 'npm ci' (vs an explicit user-typed npx). Sample the calling node process's argv. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the host, revoke all GitHub/npm/AWS/GCP tokens held by the user, and rotate any SSH keys present. Pull node_modules/<suspect-package> for IR. 3) HUNT: search for outbound to webhook.site (see Shai-Hulud beacon UC), look for new public GitHub repos under the user's account, query DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to bun.sh and github.com/oven-sh/bun, and pivot on the SHA256 of the trufflehog binary across the fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName has "trufflehog" or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "trufflehog" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe","sh","bash")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TruffleHog secret scanner spawned by npm package manager
id: 7d3f8a2e-5b1c-4e8f-9a7c-1d3e2f4b5a6c
description: Detects TruffleHog credential scanner spawned by npm/node/yarn/pnpm/bun, consistent with the Shai-Hulud npm worm credential-harvesting behavior
references:
    - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
    - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:

            - '\\pnpm.cmd'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\yarn.cmd OR *\\pnpm.cmd OR *\\bun.exe) (@CommandLine:*trufflehog* OR @CommandLine:*TruffleHog* OR @Image:*\\trufflehog* OR @Image:*\\TruffleHog*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(node\.exe|npm\.(cmd|exe)|npx\.cmd|yarn\.(cmd|exe)|pnpm\.(cmd|exe)|bun\.exe)$/i (ImageFileName=/trufflehog/i OR CommandLine=/trufflehog/i)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.exe","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe","node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","bun")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("trufflehog","trufflehog.exe") OR Processes.process="*trufflehog*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Nx s1ngularity exfil: GitHub repo 's1ngularity-repository' / 'results.b64' AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the Nx s1ngularity exfiltration pattern where the postinstall payload creates a public GitHub repository (s1ngularity-repository, sometimes numerically suffixed) under the victim's own account and commits a triple-base64-encoded credential bundle named results.b64. Surfaced via gh CLI, git, curl, or wget commandlines. Rationale: Anchored on two literal Nx s1ngularity strings ('s1ngularity-repository' and 'results.b64') corroborated by the Nx post-mortem, Datadog Security Labs, and CyberSecureFox. These strings are essentially unique — neither has a benign use. Multi-source detection (process + file) catches both the gh/git invocation and the staged bundle file. Cross-checked against: • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/learnings-from-recent-npm-compromises/ • https://cybersecurefox.com/en/nx-supply-chain-attack-s1ngularity-github-actions-npm/
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team replicating the IR scenario in a lab
  • Security researcher cloning the public s1ngularity-response repo (BunsDev/s1ngularity-response) for analysis — git clone URL would mention it
  • Threat-intel feed enrichment script that posts the literal string in a benign context
  • Incident response document containing the IOC strings opened in a script editor
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: capture the full cmdline + parent chain. Identify which GitHub account was authenticated via 'gh auth status' on the host. List public repos under that account ('gh repo list --visibility public') and check for s1ngularity-repository, s1ngularity-repository-0, ...-1, etc. 2) CONTAIN: delete the attacker-created public repos immediately (they expose credentials publicly). Revoke the GitHub PAT and all OAuth grants on that account, rotate npm/AWS/GCP keys, force-rotate SSH keypairs. Isolate the host. 3) HUNT: pivot on the user's other endpoints, search EmailEvents for any phishing that compromised the GitHub credential, and check DeviceFileEvents for ~/.gitconfig / ~/.npmrc tampering. Block 's1ngularity-repository*' as a regex in egress DLP.
union
(
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("gh.exe","git.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity-repository","results.b64")
        or (ProcessCommandLine has "repo create" and ProcessCommandLine has "--public" and ProcessCommandLine has "s1ngularity")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ActionType = "ProcessCreated",
              Evidence = strcat(FileName, " :: ", ProcessCommandLine),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
(
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "results.b64" or FolderPath has "s1ngularity-repository"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ActionType,
              Evidence = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("gh.exe","git.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where CommandLine has_any ("s1ngularity-repository","results.b64")
        or (CommandLine has "repo create" and CommandLine has "--public" and CommandLine has "s1ngularity")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, Source="4688", Evidence = CommandLine, Parent = ParentProcessName
),
(
    ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "results.b64" or TargetFilePath has "s1ngularity-repository"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, Account = ActorUsername, Source="File", Evidence = TargetFilePath, Parent = ActingProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\gh.exe OR *\\GH.EXE OR *\\git.exe OR *\\GIT.EXE OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) (@CommandLine:*s1ngularity-repository* OR @CommandLine:*results.b64* OR (@CommandLine:*"repo create"* AND @CommandLine:*--public* AND @CommandLine:*s1ngularity*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(gh|git|curl|wget|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i (CommandLine=/s1ngularity-repository|results\.b64/i OR (CommandLine=/repo create/i AND CommandLine=/--public/i AND CommandLine=/s1ngularity/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("gh.exe","git.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","gh","git")) AND (Processes.process="*s1ngularity-repository*" OR Processes.process="*results.b64*" OR (Processes.process="*repo create*" AND Processes.process="*--public*" AND Processes.process="*s1ngularity*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("gh.exe","git.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","gh","git")) AND (Processes.process="*s1ngularity-repository*" OR Processes.process="*results.b64*" OR (Processes.process="*repo create*" AND Processes.process="*--public*" AND Processes.process="*s1ngularity*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Shai-Hulud Webhook.site C2 beacon from Node/npm/Bun process AICommand & Control High
Detects outbound traffic to webhook.site, and specifically to the Shai-Hulud-attributed bundle path bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7, originating from a node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun-spawned process. webhook.site is a free request-bin service that Shai-Hulud hardcodes as its credential dropbox. Rationale: webhook.site is a confirmed hardcoded Shai-Hulud C2 endpoint per Sysdig and Checkmarx (the bb8ca5f6 token is the literal bundle ID published in their write-ups). Tagging only npm-ecosystem-spawned connections cuts the legitimate developer-testing FP volume. The ShaiHuludMarker column lets the SOC promote any hit with the literal bundle ID straight to incident. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://checkmarx.com/zero-post/inside-shai-huluds-maw-how-the-npm-worm-exploits-and-propagates/ • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm
ATT&CKT1567 T1071.001 T1102
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer testing a Stripe/Twilio/Slack webhook by curling webhook.site from a node script during local dev
  • CI pipeline using webhook.site as a request bin for integration tests
  • Postman or Insomnia desktop client (electron/node-based) hitting webhook.site
  • QA engineer running 'npm test' against a service that sends webhooks for verification
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("test","integration","e2e","jest","mocha","playwright") and not (RemoteUrl has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm whether the URL path contains 'bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7' (ShaiHuludMarker=TRUE = treat as confirmed). For non-marker hits, pull the parent npm install context — was a package being installed when the connection fired? 2) CONTAIN: isolate host, block webhook.site at the proxy/DNS for npm-ecosystem User-Agents, force-revoke all GitHub PAT / npm tokens / cloud creds on the host. 3) HUNT: hash any node_modules subdir modified in the prior 24h, search for TruffleHog spawn (see related UC), look for s1ngularity-repository creation, and pivot on the SHA256 of the bun binary if present. Add the bb8ca5f6 path to TI feed and the DLP egress block list.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "webhook.site"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| extend ShaiHuludMarker = iff(RemoteUrl has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7", "TRUE", "FALSE")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          RemoteUrl, ShaiHuludMarker, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by ShaiHuludMarker desc, Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(
    ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has "webhook.site" or Url has "webhook.site"
    | extend ShaiHuludMarker = iff(Url has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7", "TRUE", "FALSE")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="NetworkSession", Host=DvcHostname, SrcUser=SrcUsername, Dst=DstHostname, Url, ShaiHuludMarker
),
(
    DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name =~ "webhook.site" or Name endswith ".webhook.site"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="DNS", Host=Computer, SrcUser="", Dst=Name, Url="", ShaiHuludMarker="DNS-only"
)
| order by ShaiHuludMarker desc, TimeGenerated desc
title: Shai-Hulud Webhook.site Beacon from Node/npm Process
id: 8c4f1a2d-7e5b-4f3c-9a8d-2b1c3d4e5f6a
description: Detects outbound network connection to webhook.site from a node/npm/yarn/pnpm/bun-spawned process, the hardcoded C2 dropbox used by the Shai-Hulud npm worm
references:

    - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
    - attack.command_and_control
    - attack.t1071.001
    - attack.t1567
logsource:
    category: dns
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        QueryName|contains: 'webhook.site'

            - '\\node.exe'

            - '\\npm.exe'

    condition: selection

source:windows.sysmon (@EventID:3 OR @EventID:22) (@DestinationHostname:webhook.site OR @QueryName:*webhook.site*) @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\yarn.cmd OR *\\pnpm.cmd OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe)

Bun runtime fetched mid-npm-install (Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud staging) AIDelivery Medium
Detects npm/node/yarn/pnpm pulling and installing the Bun JavaScript runtime during a package install. Both Shai-Hulud (Nov 2025) and Mini Shai-Hulud (May 2026) stage the cred-stealer payload inside Bun, so an npm install that drags in Bun on a host that previously never ran it is a strong supply-chain marker. Rationale: Article explicitly says Shai-Hulud 'installed the Bun runtime during setup' and Mini Shai-Hulud 'planted a preinstall hook that pulled the Bun runtime'. The two URL signals (bun.sh/install and github.com/oven-sh/bun) are how Bun's documented installer fetches. Pairing with a node/npm parent eliminates the legitimate dev-who-runs-curl-from-shell FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
ATT&CKT1105 T1195.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or CI runner that genuinely uses Bun as a runtime and runs the official installer from a node-wrapped task
  • Devcontainer post-create script that node-bootstraps Bun on container build
  • Polyglot monorepo where one workspace runs 'npm run setup' that contains 'curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash'
  • Engineer evaluating Bun as a replacement runtime and triggering installer from a node script
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName in (dynamic(["<known-bun-dev-hosts>"])) or AccountName in (dynamic(["<known-bun-developers>"])))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: was Bun already present on this host before this event? Query DeviceInfo / DeviceFileEvents for prior bun.exe sightings on this DeviceId. If first-seen on host AND during an npm install, treat as suspect. 2) CONTAIN: stop the npm install, isolate the host, pull node_modules for IR snapshot. Revoke tokens the host had access to. 3) HUNT: check the same time window for TruffleHog spawn, webhook.site beacons, and s1ngularity-repository creation under the user's GitHub. Pivot per-host: a new bun.exe SHA256 appearing on N hosts within hours = worm propagation.
let JsPkgMgr = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe"]);
let BunSignals = dynamic(["bun.sh/install","oven-sh/bun","install.sh"]);
union
(
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr)
        or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (BunSignals) or FileName in~ ("bun.exe","bun")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              Source = "Process",
              Evidence = strcat(FileName, " :: ", ProcessCommandLine),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
),
(
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun.sh/install","oven-sh/bun")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr) or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
        or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (JsPkgMgr)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName,
              AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Source = "Network",
              Evidence = RemoteUrl,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","oven-sh/bun")
    or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "curl" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "install.sh" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "bun")
    or ActingProcessName endswith "bun.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
