Implicit node-gyp rebuild from binding.gyp during npm install AIExploitation Medium
Hunt-tier surface for the binding.gyp attack path that npm v12 closes — packages that ship a binding.gyp trigger an implicit 'node-gyp rebuild' during npm install with no script declared in package.json, executing arbitrary build code. Hunt for node-gyp invocations spawned by npm/yarn/pnpm and baseline against your approved native-module set. Rationale: The article calls out the binding.gyp attack vector explicitly: 'When a package ships a binding.gyp, npm runs an implicit node-gyp rebuild for it during install, so a dependency with a spotless package.json can still execute code just by carrying that one build file.' Aikido's own research is the second-source citation in the article. Hunting tier — node-gyp is benign for many native modules (sqlite3, sharp, bcrypt). The aggregation surfaces which native module a host is compiling so the SOC can baseline. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1027.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native modules: sqlite3, better-sqlite3, sharp, bcrypt, canvas, node-sass, node-saml, node-pty — all use binding.gyp
  • CI builder building any Electron app from source
  • Native-module rebuild after a Node major version bump (common across the fleet at once)
  • Local 'npm install' on a developer laptop pulling in any C/C++-bound package
Suppression filter
| where NativeModule !in ("sqlite3","better-sqlite3","sharp","bcrypt","canvas","node-sass","sass","node-pty","node-saml","node-expat","deasync","fsevents","keytar","node-gyp","nodegit","grpc","@grpc/grpc-js")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull NativeModule from the aggregation. If it's in your known-good native-module allowlist (sqlite3, sharp, etc.) — close. If it's an unfamiliar package name, pivot npm registry view of that package and check publish date / maintainer change history. 2) CONTAIN: only escalate if the package is unknown — quarantine the host, snapshot the node_modules/<module>/build/ artifacts. 3) HUNT: pull the module's binding.gyp from disk and inspect 'actions' / 'sources' fields for shellouts. Search the fleet for that module name across DeviceProcessEvents to scope. Cross-ref against npm v12 readiness output ('npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending').
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "node-gyp" and ProcessCommandLine has "rebuild")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "binding.gyp"
    or FileName in~ ("node-gyp.cmd","node-gyp.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend NativeModule = extract(@"node_modules[\\/]+([^\\/]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Hits = count(),
            DistinctModules = dcount(NativeModule),
            SampleModules = make_set(NativeModule, 25),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine)
            by DeviceName, AccountName
| order by FirstSeen desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (CommandLine has "node-gyp" and CommandLine has "rebuild")
    or CommandLine has "binding.gyp"
    or NewProcessName has_any ("node-gyp.cmd","node-gyp.exe")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","pnpm.cmd","bun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend NativeModule = extract(@"node_modules[\\/]+([^\\/]+)", 1, CommandLine)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Hits = count(),
            DistinctModules = dcount(NativeModule),
            SampleModules = make_set(NativeModule, 25),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine)
            by Computer, Account
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\yarn.cmd OR *\\pnpm.cmd OR *\\bun.exe) (@CommandLine:*node-gyp* OR @CommandLine:*binding.gyp*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(node\.exe|npm\.(cmd|exe)|yarn\.(cmd|exe)|pnpm\.(cmd|exe)|bun\.exe)$/i CommandLine=/node-gyp.*rebuild|binding\.gyp/i
| regex("node_modules[\\\\/]+(?<native_module>[^\\\\/]+)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, native_module], function=count())

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'

    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'

            - '\chrome.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

status: experimental

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

    vendor.

            - '\mshta.exe'

Unauthenticated POST to meta-ads-mcp /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 (CVE-2026-48039) AIExploitation High
Hunts for inbound HTTP POSTs to the /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 that succeed without an Authorization header — the exact exploitation vector for CVE-2026-48039 where AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch() forwards unauthenticated requests to downstream MCP tool handlers. Correlates with successful 200 responses to confirm tool execution rather than rejection. Rationale: Article body explicitly names the /mcp endpoint, TCP 8080 default port, and POST verb in its PoC (docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 ... POST /mcp HTTP/1.1). Combination of POST + /mcp + 8080 + 200 status + external source is the exploitation signature with near-zero benign baseline. No external sources cross-checked — advisory is the canonical source.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate internal monitoring/healthcheck POSTs from the same subnet (filter by src IP allow-list)
  • Authorized red-team or vulnerability scans against the MCP server
  • CI/CD integration tests hitting /mcp from a known build-runner IP
  • Authenticated MCP clients that don't strip the Authorization header but proxy strips it before logging
  • Internal misconfiguration where MCP is intentionally exposed to a trusted internal segment
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--host 127.0.0.1" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--host localhost" and RemoteIP !in (dynamic(["<known-monitoring-ip-1>","<known-scanner-ip-1>"]))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Pull the full request body and response for the matching session — confirm the JSON-RPC `tools/call` method invocation and inspect the response body for the substring `access_token=` in any `request_url` field (proof of token leakage). Identify the source IP, geo, and ASN; check threat-intel reputation. 2. Contain: Immediately block inbound 8080 from external networks at the perimeter firewall; if the meta-ads-mcp container is exposed (--host 0.0.0.0), restart with --host 127.0.0.1 binding or place behind an authenticated reverse proxy. Rotate the operator's META_ACCESS_TOKEN in Meta Business Manager and revoke any active sessions. 3. Hunt: Search outbound traffic from the host to graph.facebook.com for any URL containing `access_token=` (UC2); review Meta Ads activity log for unauthorized ad-account API calls during the exposure window; check for other exposed MCP servers in the estate via UC3.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionAccepted","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where LocalPort == 8080
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python.exe","python3","python","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn","docker.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","http_auth_integration")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationPort == 8080
| where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
| where RequestURL has "/mcp"
| where toint(coalesce(EventOutcome, "0")) in (200, 0) or DeviceAction !in~ ("blocked","denied","deny","drop")
| extend IsExternalSrc = not(ipv4_is_private(SourceIP))
| where IsExternalSrc == true
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 LocalPort=8080 ConnectionDirection=1
| ContextImageFileName=/(python|uvicorn|docker)/i
| regex("(meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp|http_auth_integration)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| RemoteAddressIP4!=/^(10\.|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\.|192\.168\.|127\.)/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, LocalPort, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Meta Graph API outbound URL leaking access_token in query string AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for outbound HTTPS to graph.facebook.com with `access_token=` exposed as a URL query parameter — the api.py:136 vulnerability where meta-ads-mcp appends the operator token directly to the URL rather than using an Authorization header. Captured when proxy TLS inspection is enabled or via host-side process command-line / script-content telemetry. Both pre-error (every Graph call) and post-error (token echoed back to attacker) cases are covered. Rationale: Article shows the exact leakage shape: `request_url`: `https://graph.facebook.com/v24.0/me/adaccounts?...&access_token=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789`, and api.py:136 confirms the token is appended as a URL query param on every call. Detecting `graph.facebook.com` + `access_token=` in a URL is high-fidelity — Meta's documented best practice is Authorization header, so seeing the token in a URL is itself a misconfiguration signal.
ATT&CKT1041 T1552.001 T1528
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy applications still using URL-based Graph API auth (Meta deprecated this pattern but it remains in some SDKs)
  • Developer/QA boxes running ad-hoc curl tests against Graph API
  • Marketing-automation tools that have not migrated to OAuth Bearer headers
  • Logging/observability pipelines that scrub URLs but echo the original in error messages
  • Proxy logs that capture the URL before redaction policies apply
Suppression filter
| where Url !has "client_id=" and Url !has "/oauth/access_token" and ActorUsername !in (dynamic(["<dev-test-account-1>","<known-marketing-svc>"]))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Extract the full URL and the captured `token_prefix`; cross-reference against the known operator token prefix (consult the Meta Business Manager admin to confirm which prefix maps to the production META_ACCESS_TOKEN). Identify the originating host and process. 2. Contain: Rotate the affected META_ACCESS_TOKEN immediately via Meta Business Manager — long-lived tokens are valid for 60 days. Audit any client of meta-ads-mcp that may have received the token in a JSON-RPC response. 3. Hunt: Search Meta Ads API audit logs (via Graph API `/me/business_users` activity) for actions performed by this token from non-corporate IPs in the last 30 days; look for spend manipulation, new ad-account permissions, or audience exports. Pivot to UC1 to find the unauthenticated /mcp POST that triggered the leak.
union
  (DeviceNetworkEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
   | where RemoteUrl has "graph.facebook.com"
   | where RemoteUrl has "access_token="
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="Network", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Url=RemoteUrl, RemoteIP),
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
   | where ProcessCommandLine has "graph.facebook.com" and ProcessCommandLine has "access_token="
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="Process", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Url=ProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP="")
| extend TokenPrefix = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,16})", 1, Url)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "graph.facebook.com"
| where Url has "access_token="
| extend TokenPrefix = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,16})", 1, Url)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, Url, TokenPrefix, HttpStatusCode, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@http.url:*graph.facebook.com*access_token=* OR @CommandLine:*graph.facebook.com*access_token=* OR @process.command_line:*graph.facebook.com*access_token=*)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/graph\.facebook\.com/i)

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ImageFileName], function=count())

meta-ads-mcp listener bound to non-loopback interface (0.0.0.0:8080) AIInstallation High
Hunts for meta-ads-mcp processes that bind the HTTP MCP listener to a non-loopback interface (--host 0.0.0.0, --host *, or any non-127.0.0.1 address on port 8080) — the deployment-level misconfiguration that exposes the CVE-2026-48039 vulnerable endpoint to the network. Loopback-only bindings are out of scope; this catches the prerequisite for remote exploitation. Rationale: Article impact section states 'an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the MCP server's HTTP port (default 8080)' — the prerequisite is non-loopback exposure. PoC shows the safe loopback binding (`-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080`) which intentionally limits exposure; we detect the opposite. Process-command-line pattern `meta_ads_mcp` + `--host 0.0.0.0` is article-grounded and high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Intentional deployment behind an authenticated reverse proxy where 0.0.0.0 binding is required for the proxy to reach the container (verify the proxy enforces auth)
  • Kubernetes pods where service mesh fronts the listener (binding is 0.0.0.0 but ingress is gated)
  • Internal lab/test deployments where exposure is bounded by network segmentation
  • Developer workstations running local dev containers (--host 0.0.0.0 is common but should not be allowed in production VLANs)
  • CI integration runners spinning up the server briefly for tests
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "--reverse-proxy" and DeviceName !in (dynamic(["<dev-workstation-1>","<ci-runner-1>"]))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Confirm the bind interface and port from the process command line; check `netstat -tlnp` / `ss -tlnp` (or `Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen`) to verify 8080 is actually listening on the public interface. Identify whether the host has a public IP or is behind a NAT/proxy. 2. Contain: Restart the meta-ads-mcp service with `--host 127.0.0.1` (loopback only) and place behind an authenticated reverse proxy (nginx + bearer-token auth, Traefik with forward-auth, or similar). Block inbound 8080 at the host firewall. 3. Hunt: Pivot to UC1 to check whether any external POST has already hit /mcp during the exposure window; pivot to UC2 to check whether the operator token has been seen in outbound URLs; check the version (UC4) to confirm whether the running build is in the ≤1.0.101 vulnerable range.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--host 0.0.0.0","--host *","--host 0","-h 0.0.0.0","HOST=0.0.0.0")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "--port 8080" and ProcessCommandLine !has "127.0.0.1" and ProcessCommandLine !has "localhost" and ProcessCommandLine !has "::1")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp") or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| extend CmdLine = coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| where CmdLine has_any ("--host 0.0.0.0","--host *","HOST=0.0.0.0","-h 0.0.0.0")
   or (CmdLine has "--port 8080" and CmdLine !has "127.0.0.1" and CmdLine !has "localhost")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, CmdLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp version (<=1.0.108) inventory AIReconnaissance High
Identifies hosts running meta-ads-mcp in the vulnerable range (≤1.0.101 confirmed; 1.0.102–1.0.108 lack git tags and are unconfirmed-patch) via software inventory and process command-line version banners. Output feeds an asset-priority list for patching and feeds UC3 to flag the highest-risk hosts (vulnerable version + non-loopback binding). Rationale: Article explicitly states 'Affected version: ≤ 1.0.101' and 'vuln <= 1.0.108' in the package footer. Version regex `^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$` matches the precise vulnerable range. Pulling from both TVM software inventory and live process command-lines gives both the dormant-install and actively-running signal — important because pip-installed packages can be present but not running.
ATT&CKT1518 T1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Versions 1.0.102–1.0.105 may be patched but cannot be confirmed without git tags — these will surface as potential vulnerable even if actually safe
  • Developer/CI hosts intentionally pinning an old version for regression testing
  • Vendored copies of meta-ads-mcp inside Docker base images where the image hasn't been rebuilt
  • Shadow IT installs where meta-ads-mcp was pulled into a venv outside the central inventory
  • Hosts with old `pip freeze` snapshots in inventory that no longer reflect current state
Response runbook
1. Triage: Cross-reference the output with UC3 to identify hosts that are both vulnerable AND exposed on a non-loopback interface — these are highest priority. Sort by LastSeen to find currently-running instances. 2. Contain: For exposed+vulnerable hosts, immediately apply the workaround (bind to 127.0.0.1 only, or block inbound 8080) and schedule emergency patching to ≥1.0.109 (next confirmed-fixed version per the advisory wording). 3. Hunt: For each vulnerable host, pull 90 days of UC1 (inbound /mcp POSTs) and UC2 (outbound graph.facebook.com URLs with access_token=) to establish whether exploitation has already occurred. Rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN on any host where indicators are positive.
let VulnVersionRegex = @"^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$";
let FromInventory = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
  | where SoftwareName has_any ("meta-ads-mcp","meta_ads_mcp") or (SoftwareVendor =~ "pipeboard" and SoftwareName has "mcp")
  | where SoftwareVersion matches regex VulnVersionRegex
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, Source="TVM", SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion;
let FromProcess = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
  | extend SoftwareVersion = extract(@"meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp[^0-9]*([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
  | where isnotempty(SoftwareVersion) and SoftwareVersion matches regex VulnVersionRegex
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, Source="Process", SoftwareName="meta-ads-mcp", SoftwareVersion;
union FromInventory, FromProcess
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sources=make_set(Source), Versions=make_set(SoftwareVersion) by DeviceId, DeviceName
| order by LastSeen desc
let VulnVersionRegex = @"^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$";
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-48039"
   or (SoftwareName has_any ("meta-ads-mcp","meta_ads_mcp") and SoftwareVersion matches regex VulnVersionRegex)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by TimeGenerated desc

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp", field=CommandLine, strict=false) OR regex("meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp", field=ImageFileName, strict=false)
| Version := regex("meta[_-]ads[_-]mcp[^0-9]*(?<v>[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| Version=/^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, Version], function=count())

CVE-2026-48039 PoC artifact execution (docker image meta-ads-mcp-vuln001, FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO) AIExploitation High
Detects known public-PoC artifacts for CVE-2026-48039: the `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` Docker image referenced in the advisory PoC, the literal `FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789` placeholder token shipped in the PoC environment, and execution of `poc.py` invoking the /mcp endpoint. High-confidence signal of either red-team testing or naive attacker tooling that hasn't customised the PoC. Rationale: Article PoC section names the exact strings: docker image `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001`, environment variable value `FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789`, and the script name `poc.py`. These are PoC-specific literals that any operator copy-pasting the advisory will trigger — extremely low FP outside intentional security testing.
ATT&CKT1610 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized red-team or purple-team exercise reproducing the advisory PoC
  • Internal security researchers validating the patch
  • Vulnerability-management tool that runs the PoC for verification
  • Sandbox detonation environments analysing public exploit code
  • Documentation copies of the advisory committed to internal wiki / git that get scanned by EDR script-content collectors
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in (dynamic(["<authorized-redteam-account>","<vm-validation-svc>"])) and DeviceName !in (dynamic(["<sandbox-host-1>","<security-lab-1>"]))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Identify the source — is this an authorized red-team exercise (check change-management / RoE records) or an unsanctioned execution? Pull the parent process tree to determine if it was launched interactively or via remote execution. 2. Contain: If unsanctioned, isolate the host, terminate the docker/podman container, kill the Python process, and capture container/process memory for forensics. Block egress from the host pending review. 3. Hunt: From the same source IP / user account, search for UC1 hits (POST /mcp from this host's IP), UC2 hits (graph.facebook.com URLs with access_token=) in the prior 30 days, and any other hosts in the estate that received connections from this source — the PoC may have been used to scan internal MCP servers.
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
       or (ProcessCommandLine has "poc.py" and ProcessCommandLine has "/mcp")
       or (FileName in~ ("docker.exe","docker","podman.exe","podman") and ProcessCommandLine has "META_ACCESS_TOKEN" and ProcessCommandLine has "8080")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="Process", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "poc.py" and (FolderPath has "meta" or FolderPath has "mcp")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="File", FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| extend Cmd = coalesce(TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| where Cmd has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
   or (Cmd has "poc.py" and Cmd has "/mcp")

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit update process spawning script/LOLBin child (supply-chain payload exec)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus: From external espionage to domestic targeting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER sample hash sighting (file/process/module load) · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER selective second-stage payload drop post-FireAnt update · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C&C infrastructure callback (dated IOC set) · [LLM] OceanLotus Denis/SOUNDBITE DNS tunneling — high-entropy subdomains + TXT abuse · [LLM] OceanLotus PHOREAL ICMP covert C&C — sustained outbound ICMP with non-standard payloads · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C&C infrastructure callback (dated IOC set) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections to the specific SPECTRALVIPER C&C IPs and domains documented in the ESET 2024-2026 campaigns. Each IP/domain pair is dated in the article's IOC table, so first-seen dates can be cross-referenced to suspected first-compromise time. Rationale: Uses the dated C&C table (gatewayrvcenter.com→139.180.128.42 first-seen 2025-09-20, coachcybersecurity.com→139.99.33.239 2024-07-08, mxprodesign.com→166.88.77.186 2024-07-12, power-sync-services.com→103.119.47.104 2024-07-06) plus financemachinelearning.com (article body), and the article's IOC IP block. Cross-checked against MITRE G0050/APT32 page and Elastic Security Labs 2023 SPECTRALVIPER write-up which lists overlapping OceanLotus infrastructure conventions. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel research VMs visiting known-bad domains during analysis
  • Sinkhole providers (CIRCL, Spamhaus) that have absorbed any of these domains
  • Generic VPS reuse — the IPs are on shared hosters (Vultr/OVH/Linode); a benign tenant could rotate onto an IP after OceanLotus moves off
  • Security tool scheduled IOC validation tasks pinging the indicators
  • Reverse DNS/PTR lookups by infrastructure monitoring tools
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","iexplore.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--type=utility","--headless") | where AccountName !endswith "$" and AccountName !in~ ("threatintel","soc-research")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256, command line and parent for the hitting connection — if it's a browser/legitimate tool the analyst may be researching; check that the user account isn't a known threat-intel researcher. Pivot on DeviceId across the last 90d to find prior connections to the broader OceanLotus IOC set. 2) Contain: isolate the device via Defender Live Response, block the IP/domain at perimeter and EDR network containment, force-rotate AAD tokens for the AccountName. 3) Hunt: search DeviceProcessEvents/DeviceFileEvents for the SPECTRALVIPER SHA1s on the same device, sweep your fleet for any of the 6 domains/8 IPs across the full retention window, and check if the host runs FireAnt Metakit (likely first-stage if so).

let SVIPER_DOMS = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents

SPECTRALVIPER sample hash sighting (file/process/module load) AIInstallation High
Matches the 20 SHA1s ESET attributes to SPECTRALVIPER samples observed in the FireAnt supply-chain and infrastructure-corporation campaigns. Any sighting in execution, file write, or DLL load telemetry is treated as confirmed OceanLotus presence. Rationale: Direct match against the 20 SHA1 hashes in the article's IOC block. Three telemetry views — process create, file write, image load — catch the binary regardless of whether it executes standalone, is dropped to disk, or is side-loaded as a DLL (OceanLotus's known DLL side-load TTP per MITRE G0050). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
ATT&CKT1059 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandboxing/EDR/AV tools writing the sample for analysis on a research VM
  • VirusTotal/Hybrid-Analysis intel ingestion writing samples to disk in a research path
  • Honeypot detonation infrastructure
  • Backup of a previously infected machine being restored containing dormant copies of the binary
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !contains "\\Quarantine\\" and FolderPath !contains "\\Sandbox\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","SenseIR.exe","hybrid-analysis-collector.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree around the SHA1 sighting — Defender DeviceProcessEvents with ProcessId/ProcessCreationTime/InitiatingProcess* to identify how the binary got onto the host (FireAnt update? signed installer DLL side-load? scheduled task?). 2) Contain: EDR-isolate the host, quarantine the file by hash org-wide via Defender file blocking, force credential rotation for the AccountName and all logged-on users in the previous 30d (DeviceLogonEvents). 3) Hunt: sweep DeviceNetworkEvents on the same DeviceId for the C&C IPs/domains in UC1, check DeviceProcessEvents/DeviceFileEvents for FireAnt Metakit presence, and run UC4/UC5 against the same host to identify Denis (DNS) or PHOREAL (ICMP) auxiliary implants.

FireAnt Metakit update process spawning script/LOLBin child (supply-chain payload exec) AIDelivery Medium
FireAnt Metakit's updater was compromised between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026 and pushed SPECTRALVIPER to selected investors. Hunts the post-update execution chain: the FireAnt updater spawning script engines / LOLBins / unsigned binaries from a writable user directory — the exact shape of a poisoned-updater payload drop. Rationale: Anchored on the FireAnt Metakit campaign (article: 'compromised the update server of FireAnt Metakit ... replaced legitimate software updates with a malicious payload that ultimately deployed SPECTRALVIPER', Oct 2025-Mar 2026). The detection key is the parent-image string match on FireAnt/Metakit because the legitimate updater should never spawn script engines or LOLBins. We treat it as hunting because we have no leaked binary name from the article — pattern match on the product name is the best available pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FireAnt updater calling msiexec for a legitimate signed MSI patch
  • FireAnt support utility spawning cmd to gather diagnostic info during a user-initiated 'send logs' action
  • Group Policy / SCCM removing a FireAnt installation by invoking msiexec under the FireAnt installer path
  • Endpoint security agent re-parented onto the FireAnt process tree mid-scan
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !has "--diagnostic" and ChildCmd !has "\\logs\\" and not (Child =~ "msiexec.exe" and ChildCmd has "/quiet" and ChildCmd has "FireAnt")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the SHA256 of both parent (FireAnt binary) and child against VirusTotal and the SPECTRALVIPER SHA1 list from UC2 — the article notes the malicious update was distributed Oct 2025 to Mar 2026, so any hit in that window is high-priority. Identify the user's role (stock investor / finance), aligning with the campaign's victim profile. 2) Contain: isolate the device, block the FireAnt parent SHA256 if confirmed malicious, file an abuse notification with FireAnt (article notes ESET tried and 'received no response' — escalate via national CERT VNCERT). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC1 (C&C IPs/domains) and UC2 (sample SHA1s) on the same host, sweep all hosts running FireAnt Metakit (DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory where SoftwareName has "FireAnt") for the same parent SHA256 across Oct 2025-Mar 2026.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "fireant" 
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit","fireant")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit","fireantapp")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or (FolderPath has_any ("\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Roaming\\","\\ProgramData\\","\\Users\\Public\\") and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "FireAnt")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentFolder = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = FileName,
          ChildFolder = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, SHA1
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
| where ParentProcessName has "fireant" or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Roaming\\","\\ProgramData\\","\\Users\\Public\\") and ActingProcessFileCompany !has "FireAnt")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA1, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Updater Spawning LOLBin or Script Engine
id: 9d2b6c4f-1a3b-4e7f-9c0d-2b8f4a1e6d22
description: OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER post-supply-chain execution chain — FireAnt Metakit updater (compromised Oct 2025-Mar 2026) spawning script interpreters or LOLBins.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent_fireant:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - '\FireAnt'
      - '\Metakit'
      - '\fireant'
  child_suspicious:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'

      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  condition: parent_fireant and child_suspicious
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\FireAnt* OR *\\fireant* OR *\\Metakit* OR *\\metakit*) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RunDLL32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/fireant|metakit/i
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|mshta|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget|msiexec)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(@timestamp, as=first_seen)])
ENDPOINT

OceanLotus Denis/SOUNDBITE DNS tunneling — high-entropy subdomains + TXT abuse AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the signature of OceanLotus's Denis (aka SOUNDBITE) backdoor, which the article names as implementing DNS tunneling for C&C. Surfaces hosts emitting many distinct high-entropy subdomains under a single parent, or sustained TXT-record queries — both characteristic of DNS-tunneled command/exfiltration. Rationale: Article explicitly names Denis/SOUNDBITE as an OceanLotus tool 'implementing DNS tunneling for C&C communications'. We hunt the canonical DNS-tunnel shape: many unique high-entropy subdomains under a single parent within a short window, plus TXT-record abuse. Allowlist baseline CDN/cloud parents to keep noise manageable. Threshold (30 distinct subs, avg length 25) is from the BluRaven baseline reference; tune per environment. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0157/
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Telemetry agents (Datadog, Splunk UF, New Relic) that use long unique session-id subdomains for cache-busting
  • Cisco Umbrella / Zscaler reverse-DNS health checks
  • Anti-spam DKIM/DMARC lookups (DKIM selectors look like high-entropy subdomains)
  • Akamai/CloudFront/Fastly CDNs that mint per-asset hostnames
  • DNS-based ad-blocker or AV update channels (e.g., Sophos LiveProtection's hash queries)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("datadog-agent.exe","splunk-uf.exe","NewRelic.Server.exe","umbrella-deployment.exe","AmpDaemon.exe") and Parent !endswith ".akamaiedge.net" and Parent !endswith ".datadoghq.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate the InitiatingProcessFileName driving the queries — legitimate svchost.exe doing DKIM lookups vs. an unsigned binary doing TXT queries are night-and-day. Pivot the same DeviceId to UC1 to see whether it also hit known SPECTRALVIPER C&C. 2) Contain: if the process is unsigned or matches UC2 hash list, EDR-isolate; block the parent domain at recursive resolver. 3) Hunt: pull DeviceProcessEvents for the InitiatingProcessId to identify the binary path, capture the binary for malware analysis, and search the fleet for the same parent domain (UC1-style IOC sweep) since Denis/SOUNDBITE C&C domains are typically reused.
let WindowSize = 1h;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Labels = split(RemoteUrl, ".")
| extend LabelCount = array_length(Labels)
| where LabelCount >= 3
| extend Sub = tostring(Labels[0])
| extend Parent = strcat(tostring(Labels[LabelCount-2]), ".", tostring(Labels[LabelCount-1]))
| extend SubLen = strlen(Sub)
| where Parent !in ("in-addr.arpa","ip6.arpa","google.com","microsoft.com","windows.com","office.com","akamaiedge.net","cloudfront.net","amazonaws.com")
| summarize TotalQueries = count(),
            DistinctSubs = dcount(Sub),
            AvgSubLen    = avg(SubLen),
            MaxSubLen    = max(SubLen),
            SampleQueries = make_set(RemoteUrl, 5)
           by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, Parent, bin(Timestamp, WindowSize)
| where DistinctSubs >= 30 and AvgSubLen >= 25
| order by DistinctSubs desc
let WindowSize = 1h;
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(DnsQuery)
| extend Labels = split(DnsQuery, ".")
| extend LabelCount = array_length(Labels)
| where LabelCount >= 3
| extend Sub = tostring(Labels[0])
| extend Parent = strcat(tostring(Labels[LabelCount-2]), ".", tostring(Labels[LabelCount-1]))
| extend SubLen = strlen(Sub)
| where Parent !in ("in-addr.arpa","ip6.arpa","google.com","microsoft.com","windows.com","office.com","akamaiedge.net","cloudfront.net","amazonaws.com")
| summarize TotalQueries = count(),
            DistinctSubs = dcount(Sub),
            AvgSubLen    = avg(SubLen),
            MaxSubLen    = max(SubLen),
            TxtCount     = countif(DnsQueryTypeName =~ "TXT"),
            SampleQueries = make_set(DnsQuery, 5)
           by SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Parent, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowSize)
| where (DistinctSubs >= 30 and AvgSubLen >= 25) or TxtCount >= 50
| order by DistinctSubs desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:22 @QueryName:* -@QueryName:(*.in-addr.arpa OR *.ip6.arpa OR *.windows.com OR *.microsoft.com OR *.office.com OR *.google.com OR *.akamaiedge.net OR *.cloudfront.net OR *.amazonaws.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName!=/\.(in-addr\.arpa|ip6\.arpa|windows\.com|microsoft\.com|office\.com|google\.com|akamaiedge\.net|cloudfront\.net|amazonaws\.com)$/i
| firstLabel := splitString(field=DomainName, by="\\.", index=0)
| firstLabelLen := length(firstLabel)
| timeBucket(span=1h)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, _bucket], function=[count(as=total), count(field=firstLabel, distinct=true, as=distinctSubs), avg(firstLabelLen, as=avgSubLen)])
| distinctSubs >= 30
| avgSubLen >= 25
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count dc(DNS.query) as unique_queries values(DNS.record_type) as record_types from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*.*" by DNS.src DNS.query bin(_time, 1h) | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | rex field=query "^(?<sub>[^\.]+)\.(?<parent>.+)$" | eval sub_len=len(sub) | stats sum(count) as total_qs dc(query) as distinct_subs avg(sub_len) as avg_sub_len max(sub_len) as max_sub_len values(record_types) as record_types by src parent _time | where distinct_subs >= 30 AND avg_sub_len >= 25 AND parent!="in-addr.arpa" AND parent!="ip6.arpa"
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(DNS.query) as unique_queries values(DNS.record_type) as record_types from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*.*" by DNS.src DNS.query bin(_time, 1h) | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | rex field=query "^(?<sub>[^\.]+)\.(?<parent>.+)$" | eval sub_len=len(sub) | stats sum(count) as total_qs dc(query) as distinct_subs avg(sub_len) as avg_sub_len max(sub_len) as max_sub_len values(record_types) as record_types by src parent _time | where distinct_subs >= 30 AND avg_sub_len >= 25 AND parent!="in-addr.arpa" AND parent!="ip6.arpa"
OceanLotus PHOREAL ICMP covert C&C — sustained outbound ICMP with non-standard payloads AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts OceanLotus's PHOREAL backdoor, which the article identifies as leveraging the ICMP protocol for C&C. Surfaces sustained outbound ICMP from endpoints to public IPs, especially correlated with non-ICMP-emitting processes (PHOREAL uses raw sockets to embed C&C in ping payloads). Rationale: Article explicitly names PHOREAL as an OceanLotus backdoor 'leveraging the ICMP protocol for C&C communications'. Detection logic: outbound ICMP from a non-utility process to a public IP, sustained over 30 minutes with 30+ events — way outside normal Windows ICMP profile (legitimate ICMP is dominated by ping.exe one-shots and network monitoring tools). Allowlists exclude ping/tracert/pathping which legitimately use ICMP. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0158/
ATT&CKT1071 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Network monitoring tools (PRTG, SolarWinds, Nagios) installed on Windows endpoints doing perimeter health pings
  • Custom in-house monitoring scripts that ping external SLAs/uptime endpoints from workstations
  • Sophos/Cisco AnyConnect doing peer-tunnel ICMP keepalives that show as public destinations pre-tunnel
  • Smokeping or RIPE Atlas probes installed for network research
  • Misconfigured load balancer / VPN client doing ICMP path MTU discovery
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("prtg probe.exe","PRTGProbe.exe","SolarWinds.Pingdom.exe","WhatsUp Gold.exe","Nagios.exe","smokeping.exe","vpnagent.exe","AnyConnect.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessFileName/SHA256 — legitimate monitoring tools (PRTG agent, SolarWinds) are obvious; anything unsigned/unknown writing raw ICMP is high-priority. Pivot to UC1/UC2 on the same DeviceId to check for known OceanLotus IOCs. 2) Contain: if the process is unknown, EDR-isolate the host and block ICMP egress from the workstation VLAN at the firewall (most workstations don't need outbound ICMP). 3) Hunt: capture the binary for malware analysis, sweep the fleet for the same InitiatingProcessSHA256, and pull a pcap on the next observed ICMP burst — PHOREAL embeds C&C in the ping payload which a packet capture will surface as non-zero, non-standard echo data.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Protocol =~ "Icmp"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("system","")
   and InitiatingProcessFileName !endswith "ping.exe"
   and InitiatingProcessFileName !endswith "tracert.exe"
   and InitiatingProcessFileName !endswith "pathping.exe"
| summarize IcmpEvents = count(),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            DurationMin = datetime_diff('minute', max(Timestamp), min(Timestamp)),
            RemoteIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 10)
           by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where IcmpEvents >= 30 and DurationMin >= 30
| order by IcmpEvents desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where NetworkProtocol =~ "ICMP" or NetworkProtocol == "1"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254." and DstIpAddr !startswith "127."
| summarize IcmpEvents = count(),
            DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(DstIpAddr),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated),
            DurationMin = datetime_diff('minute', max(TimeGenerated), min(TimeGenerated)),
            RemoteIPs = make_set(DstIpAddr, 10)
           by SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, EventProduct
| where IcmpEvents >= 30 and DurationMin >= 30
| order by IcmpEvents desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Protocol:icmp -@Image:(*\\ping.exe OR *\\PING.EXE OR *\\tracert.exe OR *\\TRACERT.EXE OR *\\pathping.exe)
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP6) Protocol=1
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(ping|tracert|pathping)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=[count(as=icmp_pkts), min(@timestamp, as=first_seen), max(@timestamp, as=last_seen)])
| icmp_pkts >= 30
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, protocol, packets, bytes, action
| filter protocol = 1 and action = "ACCEPT"
| filter dstAddr not like /^10\./ and dstAddr not like /^192\.168\./ and dstAddr not like /^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\./
| stats sum(packets) as icmp_packets, count_distinct(dstAddr) as distinct_dsts, min(@timestamp) as first_seen, max(@timestamp) as last_seen by srcAddr, dstAddr
| filter icmp_packets >= 30
| sort icmp_packets desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.transport="icmp" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | stats sum(count) as icmp_pkts dc(dest) as distinct_dests min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(app) as process by src dest | where icmp_pkts >= 30
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.transport="icmp" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.app _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | stats sum(count) as icmp_pkts dc(dest) as distinct_dests min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(app) as process by src dest | where icmp_pkts >= 30
SPECTRALVIPER selective second-stage payload drop post-FireAnt update AIInstallation Medium
Article notes that despite broad FireAnt user exposure, 'only a few individuals who ultimately received SPECTRALVIPER' — implying a victim-selection check followed by a second-stage write. Hunts file drops to user-writable persistence paths by FireAnt-spawned processes, capturing the moment selective targeting promotes from staged dropper to active backdoor. Rationale: Article body: 'only a few individuals who ultimately received SPECTRALVIPER, indicating selective targeting' — the dropper checks the victim, then writes the payload. We detect the moment of stage-2 commitment: the FireAnt updater (parent string match on FireAnt/Metakit) writing an executable/script to a writable path, OR setting a Run-key value. Unioning file-drop + autorun-write captures both deployment paths a custom backdoor with 'orchestration capabilities' (article) would use. Cross-checked against MITRE G0050 which lists T1547.001 as a known OceanLotus persistence technique. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper
ATT&CKT1105 T1547.001 T1574.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FireAnt legitimate updater writing a real signed patch DLL/EXE to its own install path (allowlist by signature)
  • FireAnt logging component writing .log-renamed-to-.txt files (extension allowlist excludes .log)
  • User installing a FireAnt plugin/extension that legitimately drops to AppData
  • FireAnt crash dump writer creating .dmp files (extension allowlist excludes .dmp)
  • Enterprise MDM repackaging FireAnt and dropping config files
Suppression filter
| where DroppedFile !endswith ".log" and DroppedFile !endswith ".dmp" and DroppedFile !endswith ".tmp" and DroppedPath !contains "\\FireAnt\\Updates\\Verified\\" and not (DroppedSHA256 in (dynamic([])) )
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SHA256 of both the parent (FireAnt binary) and the dropped file. If the dropped SHA matches the UC2 SPECTRALVIPER hash list — confirmed incident, escalate to IR immediately. Otherwise, submit dropped file to detonation. Note the AccountName: article suggests stock investors and infrastructure/transport corp employees are the target profile. 2) Contain: EDR-isolate the host, quarantine the dropped file by SHA256 across the fleet, block the parent FireAnt binary hash if confirmed malicious. 3) Hunt: from the same DeviceId, run UC1 (C&C beacons) and UC4/UC5 (Denis DNS / PHOREAL ICMP), sweep DeviceFileEvents fleet-wide for the dropped SHA256, and pull DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory for the FireAnt version on impacted hosts to identify the malicious update package version.
let SuspiciousExtensions = dynamic([".exe",".dll",".bat",".ps1",".vbs",".js",".hta",".lnk",".scr"]);
let WritablePaths = dynamic(["\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\","\\AppData\\Roaming\\","\\ProgramData\\","\\Users\\Public\\","\\Windows\\Temp\\"]);
let FireAntFileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName has "fireant"
     or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
  | where FolderPath has_any (WritablePaths)
  | extend Ext = tolower(strcat(".", tostring(split(FileName, ".")[-1])))
  | where Ext in (SuspiciousExtensions)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            DroppedFile = FileName, DroppedPath = FolderPath, DroppedSHA1 = SHA1, DroppedSHA256 = SHA256,
            Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, DeviceId;
let FireAntRunKey = DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
  | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
  | where RegistryKey has_any ("\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce","\\Image File Execution Options\\","\\AppInit_DLLs")
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName has "fireant"
     or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
            Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, DeviceId;
union FireAntFileWrites, FireAntRunKey
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspiciousExtensions = dynamic([".exe",".dll",".bat",".ps1",".vbs",".js",".hta",".lnk",".scr"]);
let WritablePaths = dynamic(["\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\","\\AppData\\Roaming\\","\\ProgramData\\","\\Users\\Public\\","\\Windows\\Temp\\"]);
let FireAntWrites = ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
  | where ActingProcessName has "fireant" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
  | where TargetFilePath has_any (WritablePaths)
  | extend Ext = tolower(TargetFileExtension)
  | where strcat(".", Ext) in (SuspiciousExtensions)
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername,
            DroppedFile=TargetFileName, DroppedPath=TargetFilePath, DroppedSHA1=TargetFileSHA1, DroppedSHA256=TargetFileSHA256,
            Parent=ActingProcessName, ParentCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine;
let FireAntRunKey = ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
  | where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
  | where RegistryKey has_any ("\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce","\\Image File Execution Options\\","\\AppInit_DLLs")
  | where ActingProcessName has "fireant" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, User=ActorUsername,
            DroppedFile=RegistryValue, DroppedPath=RegistryKey, DroppedSHA1="", DroppedSHA256="",
            Parent=ActingProcessName, ParentCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine;
union FireAntWrites, FireAntRunKey
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Updater Writing Executable Payload or Run-Key (SPECTRALVIPER Stage 2)
id: a3f7d9c1-8b4e-4d2f-9f0e-3c2d1b4e5a99
description: Detects the second-stage payload drop from OceanLotus FireAnt Metakit supply-chain compromise (Oct 2025-Mar 2026) — the FireAnt updater writing PE/script files to user-writable persistence paths or setting Run-key autostarts. Article notes only a subset of FireAnt users received SPECTRALVIPER, suggesting selective second-stage delivery.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/19
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    Image|contains:
      - '\FireAnt'
      - '\fireant'
      - '\Metakit'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.exe'
      - '.dll'
      - '.bat'
      - '.ps1'
      - '.vbs'
      - '.js'
      - '.hta'
      - '.lnk'
      - '.scr'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\FireAnt* OR *\\fireant* OR *\\Metakit* OR *\\metakit*) @TargetFilename:(*\\AppData\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\*) @TargetFilename:(*.exe OR *.dll OR *.bat OR *.ps1 OR *.vbs OR *.js OR *.hta OR *.lnk OR *.scr)
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten OR #event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate) ContextImageFileName=/fireant|metakit/i
| (TargetFileName=/\\(AppData|ProgramData|Users\\Public|Windows\\Temp)\\/i AND TargetFileName=/\.(exe|dll|bat|ps1|vbs|js|hta|lnk|scr)$/i) OR RegObjectName=/\\(CurrentVersion\\Run|CurrentVersion\\RunOnce|Image File Execution Options|AppInit_DLLs)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, RegObjectName, RegStringValue], function=[count(), min(@timestamp, as=first_seen)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as first_seen values(Filesystem.file_name) as file_name values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.process_name="*fireant*" OR Filesystem.process_path="*FireAnt*" OR Filesystem.process_path="*Metakit*") AND Filesystem.file_name IN ("*.exe","*.dll","*.bat","*.ps1","*.vbs","*.js","*.hta") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as first_seen values(Filesystem.file_name) as file_name values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.process_name="*fireant*" OR Filesystem.process_path="*FireAnt*" OR Filesystem.process_path="*Metakit*") AND Filesystem.file_name IN ("*.exe","*.dll","*.bat","*.ps1","*.vbs","*.js","*.hta") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount

DeviceProcessEvents

| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
